summary: Eight adversarial rounds against a command that deletes a directory tree inside someone else's repository. Every confirmed path to deleting unshipped content or reading outside the target was closed; the final pass reports no in-scope defect remaining (0.96). The dominant class was repository escape through symlinks — found at the leaf, at the skills root, at the machinery root, and through ancestors of the report's own reads.

non_blocking_findings.summary: Preservation dereferenced symlinks (copytree defaults to symlinks=False, copy2 follows), so a link's referent was copied into the repo under the link's name while retirement deleted the original. Fixed at both keep and restore.

A symlinked .agents/skills root passed is_dir() and had iterdir() walk the referent; a symlinked .agents root did the same one level up while validation returned silently. Both refused before any write.
The stale-reference report read working-tree bytes, so a symlinked ancestor (reachable with --force) redirected reads outside the repo. Now searches the git index, which resolves paths itself.

Content was exempted from the counterpart check by naming convention: first anything under a __pycache__ directory, then any .pyc by suffix. Both let tracked client content be deleted on nothing but its name. Narrowed to untracked bytecode.

The refusal instructed the human to delete the offending path and re-run, but aborted AFTER the trees were replaced — so the re-run hit the dirty-target gate. Validation moved ahead of the first write.
A non-directory .agents/skills root, and a dangling tracked skill symlink, were each skipped by validation and by preservation, then deleted with the tree. Both now refuse or preserve.

After this review was recorded, upgrade.py changed once: it read the target's project-owned harness.yaml unconditionally and crashed on a legacy repo that has none — the normal case for the repos this command upgrades — after the writes had landed. Fixed in PR #37, covered by a regression test, local autoreview clean at 0.95, and verified end to end against a real legacy repo. Recorded here so this artifact does not read as having reviewed code it predates.

residual_risks: D-0002: a client skill whose name the harness has since started shipping is replaced rather than preserved under conflict. Not decidable from paths — the harness ships factory/skills/forge.md, so refusing every collision refuses every upgrade, and an older harness's copy differs from a client's exactly the way a client's would. Not silent: upgrade refuses a dirty tree, so the replacement lands as a reviewed deletion in the upgrade diff.
The stale-reference report is advisory and index-based. Under --force the clean-tree invariant does not hold, and the report says so rather than claiming a definitive answer.
